terms.definition: A polyhedron with two congruent parallel polygonal bases joined by parallelogram faces.
A solid with two congruent parallel circular bases connected by a curved surface.
Solids with equal heights and equal cross-sectional areas at every corresponding height have equal volumes.
The shortest distance measured at a right angle between a base plane and its opposite base or apex.
A polyhedron with one polygonal base and triangular faces meeting at an apex.
A solid with a circular base and a curved surface tapering to an apex.
The set of all points in space a fixed distance from a center.
A two-dimensional arrangement of faces that can fold to form a three-dimensional solid.
The area of a solid's side surfaces excluding designated base or bases.
The total area of all exterior surfaces of a three-dimensional solid.
A surface distance from a pyramid or cone apex toward its base, used in lateral-area formulas.
The distance around a circle; 2πr, and the width of an unwrapped cylinder's lateral rectangle.
The two-dimensional figure formed where a plane intersects a three-dimensional solid.
A circular cross-section of a sphere made by a plane through the sphere's center.
The fixed line around which a planar region rotates to generate a solid of revolution.
A three-dimensional solid generated by rotating a planar region about an axis.
The multiplicative ratio k relating corresponding linear measures in similar figures or solids.
For similar solids, lengths scale by k, surface areas by k², and volumes by k³.
The amount of three-dimensional space occupied by a solid, measured in cubic units.
